The board
Hi! Let's learn chess.
It's played on a board with 64 squares, light and dark. Two players: White and Black. White always starts.
Now you know the board!
This is how a game starts. Each player has 16 pieces. You have White, the ones near you.
Every square has a name: a letter and a number, like in Battleship.
The rook
The rook goes in a straight line: forwards, backwards and sideways. As far as it likes.
But it can't jump over other pieces.
The rook goes in a straight line.
Take the rook to the star.
Now collect the two stars.
Collect the three stars.
Your pawns are in the way. The rook can't jump them. Find another way!
The bishop
The bishop goes diagonally, as if it were cutting the squares through the corners. As far as it likes.
That's why it always steps on squares of the same colour.
The bishop goes diagonally.
Take the bishop to the star.
Collect the two stars.
This bishop only steps on light squares. Collect the three stars.
A pawn is in the way. Find another!
The queen
The queen is the strongest piece of all.
She can go in a straight line, like the rook, and diagonally, like the bishop.
The queen goes straight and diagonally.
Collect the four stars in as few moves as you can.
The king
The king is the most important piece. You must take good care of it!
But it walks slowly: just one square at a time, in any direction.
The king walks one square at a time.
Take the king to the star.
Collect the two stars, step by step.
Collect the two stars. The king can also go diagonally.
The knight
The knight jumps making an L: two squares one way and one more the other way.
It's the only piece that can jump over the others.
The knight jumps making an L.
Take the knight to the star.
The knight jumps over your pawns!
The pawn
The pawn walks forward, one square. The first time it moves, it can go two.
It never goes backwards. And to capture, it goes diagonally.
The pawn walks straight and captures diagonally.
The first time, the pawn can move two squares. Do it in one go!
Capture the two black pieces. Remember: the pawn captures diagonally.
Capture the three pieces. Look carefully at which way the pawn captures.
Capturing
Capturing is taking your piece to the square of an opponent's piece. You remove it from the board and stand in its place.
Capturing is taking away an opponent's piece.
Capture the two black pieces with the rook.
Capture the three pieces with the bishop.
Capture the three pieces with the knight.
Capture the four pieces with the queen, in as few moves as you can.
Don't get captured!
The black pieces can capture too.
Before moving, check whether the square you're going to is attacked.
Before moving, look at what your opponent attacks.
Capture the two pieces without getting captured. Which one do you start with?
The black pawn protects the knight. Capture both without losing your queen.
Capture the three pieces. Watch out for the black pawns!
What each piece is worth
Some pieces are worth more than others. The pawn is worth 1. The knight and bishop, 3. The rook, 5. And the queen, 9.
The king can never be captured.
The queen is worth more than all the others.
You can capture three pieces. Take the most valuable one!
That move doesn't capture anything. Try another!
The knight is worth 3. Another one is worth more.
The pawn is worth 1. Another one is worth more.
Good! The rook is worth 5: it's the most valuable.
The knight can capture three pieces. Which one do you take?
Good! The queen is worth 9: it's the most valuable.
The pawn can capture on both sides. Choose well!
Check
Giving check is attacking your opponent's king. When their king is in check, they have to save it right away.
Check is attacking the king.
Give check to the black king with the rook.
That move doesn't attack the black king. Try another!
Check! With your rook you attack the black king.
Give check with the bishop.
Check! With your bishop you attack the black king.
Give check with the knight.
Check! With your knight you attack the black king.
Getting out of check
There are three ways to save the king from check: move it, capture the attacking piece, or put another piece in between.
The king is saved by moving, capturing or blocking.
Your king is in check! Here you can only save it by moving it.
Good! You saved your king by moving it.
Check again! Now capture the attacking piece.
Good! You saved your king by capturing the attacking piece.
And now, put a piece in between.
Good! You saved your king by blocking the check.
Checkmate
Checkmate is a check the king can't be saved from. Whoever gives checkmate wins the game!
Checkmate means winning!
Give checkmate. The black pawns don't let their king escape.
That move doesn't give check. Try another!
Checkmate! The black king can't be saved.
Give checkmate with the queen. Your king helps her.
It's check, but the black king can escape. Try another!
Give checkmate with the knight.
Give checkmate with the rook.
Stalemate
Careful: if the opponent's king isn't in check but can't move anywhere, it's stalemate. And then it's a draw.
Stalemate is a draw. Careful!
Look: it's the black king's turn. It isn't in check, but it can't move anywhere. That's stalemate, and it's a draw! Tap «Why?».
Another stalemate: the black king isn't in check, but your pawn and your king take away all its squares.
Give checkmate. But don't stalemate it!
Stalemate! The black king isn't in check, but it can't move. That's a draw.
Again: checkmate, without stalemating it.
It's check, but that piece can be captured. Try another!
Castling
Castling is a special move: you move the king and the rook at the same time, to hide the king.
To do it, move the king two squares towards the rook. The rook jumps to the other side by itself.
With castling, the king hides.
Castle towards the nearest rook.
To castle, move the king two squares towards the rook.
Castled! Your king is now hidden.
That castling goes to the other side.
Now do it to the other side.
Promotion
If a pawn gets all the way to the end of the board, it turns into another piece! Almost always a queen.
A pawn that reaches the end becomes a queen.
Take the pawn all the way to the end and turn it into a queen.
You can, but the queen is the strongest. Choose queen!
Promoted! Your pawn is now a queen.
Take the pawn to the end of the board.
Capture and promote at the same time.
En passant
This move is a bit unusual. If an opponent's pawn moves two squares and stops next to yours, you can capture it as if it had moved only one.
But only right at that moment.
En passant: only right afterwards.
The black pawn has just moved two squares. Capture it en passant!
Move your pawn diagonally, just behind the black pawn.
En passant! You captured the black pawn.
Again: the black pawn has just arrived. Take advantage!
